title: Sunny and the Boobook Owl
description: Little Sonny the quokka hears the soft call of a boobook owl on a still, starry night. A gentle, wonder-filled bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
It was a still night in the bush, and Sunny couldn't sleep.

He lay on his mossy rock and looked up at the sky. The stars were very bright. The moon was a thin silver crescent, barely a sliver. The air was cool and clean.

And then — from somewhere high in the trees — a sound.

Boo-book.

Soft. Low. Twice.

Boo-book.

Sunny sat up.

He looked into the darkness of the trees, but he couldn't see anything. Just the silhouettes of branches and leaves against the star-thick sky.

Boo-book.

He waited, very still, breathing quietly.

And then — there. A shape, round-headed and patient, sitting on a branch not too far away. A small owl, barely bigger than Sunny's head, watching the night with huge golden eyes.

The boobook owl turned its head to look at Sunny.

Sunny looked back.

For a long, still moment, they simply regarded each other through the soft darkness.

The owl blinked. Sunny blinked.

Boo-book, said the owl, very quietly, as if it was just making conversation.

Sunny nodded, even though he had no idea what that meant. It seemed like the right thing to do.

The owl looked away then, back out into the darkness of the bush. Patient. Watching. At home in the nighttime in a way that Sunny envied just a little.

Sunny lay back on his rock. The stars spun slowly above him.

From the trees, soft and steady:

Boo-book. Boo-book.

Sunny closed his eyes and let the sound carry him toward sleep.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, boobook owl. Goodnight, dark and beautiful night.
